definition: The change from liquid water into water vapour, a gas. It happens when heat breaks the bonds that hold water molecules together.
Water in the form of a gas. It is invisible, and it mixes into the air.
The change from water vapour back into liquid water. It is the opposite of evaporation.
The temperature air has to cool to before its water vapour starts to condense into liquid water.
Tiny particles in the air, such as dust, salt, smoke and pollen, that water vapour condenses on to form cloud droplets.
Water released from clouds as rain, freezing rain, sleet, snow or hail.
Droplets bumping into each other and merging into bigger drops.
Air moving upward inside a cloud. A drop falls out of the cloud only when it falls faster than the updraft.
The way ice crystals in a cloud grow quickly by taking water from the cloud, then fall as snow or melt into rain.
